checks.detail: GNNExplainer picks out a troll's ring edges with AUC 0.69 (0.5 = chance); needs 0.70.

strengths.text: Accurate: test AUC 0.965, within 0.000 of the reference 0.965.
Integrated Gradients is faithful: removing the inputs flagged as important really does move the score.

weaknesses.text: Explanations barely find a troll's ring edges (best AUC 0.69, 0.50 = chance).
Acts largely as a degree counter: its score has rank correlation 0.83 with how many connections an account has (degree alone scores AUC 0.91).
GNNExplainer and Integrated Gradients disagree on what matters (rank agreement 0.29): at least one of them is misleading.
GNNExplainer gives a different answer when re-run on the same account (rank agreement between runs: GNNExplainer 0.65).

checklist.text: Test on data collected after your training data. Behaviour drifts, and a validation split from the same period hides that.
Choose the decision threshold on held-out data for the precision you need; a wrongly banned real user costs more than a missed bot.
Keep a fixed audit sample of labelled accounts and re-run the explanations on it after every retrain.
List which inputs an attacker can change cheaply (posting rate, hashtags, timing) and test the model with those changed.
Do not rely on edge explanations to identify coordinated groups; verify rings with a separate method.
checklist.because: Explanations barely find a troll's ring edges (best AUC 0.69, 0.50 = chance).

checklist.text: Test on popular real accounts: a model that counts connections will flag them.
